column6: Core Idea said step 1 "releasing the intron lariat"; step 1 forms the lariat intermediate and step 2 releases it (as the Explainer says). Changed to "forming".
Not fixed, older text: Q1 explanation's NAD+/fermentation reasoning about the citric acid cycle is muddled but not clearly false.
essential kept: it is the technical term (essential amino acid), not filler.
Worked the two cycles: tripeptidyl-tRNA in P and 4 GTP (2 EF-Tu, 2 EF-G); the count excludes initiation GTP.

Explainer said "the amino acid in the P site is transferred" onto the A-site amino acid; the whole growing chain on the P-site tRNA is transferred (this contradicted the new misconception bullet 1). Minimal edit.

Exercise "how" was broken when worked: blocking each of the 5 enzymes had only 3 answer options (carbamoyl phosphate, citrulline, arginine). CPS I block builds up ammonia and ASL block builds up argininosuccinate. Added both to the list.

Not fixed, older text: Explainer says the cycle runs "exclusively" in hepatocytes and says every enzyme defect gives neonatal hyperammonemia (arginase deficiency usually does not); both are overstated but left as is.
